question.problem:
For $x,y,z\in {R}^{2},$ consider the following functions: 

$$
\begin{aligned} & y(x)=Ax\,\text{where}\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & z(y)=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}^{2} \\ {y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & f(z)=Cz\,\text{where}\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $z\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $C$ and outputs a vector $f(z)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}=C.
$$

- The function $z$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ and outputs a vector $z(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & 2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating at ${y}_{0}=A{x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}2(1) & 0 \\ 0 & 2(3)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $A$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=A.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x))){|}_{{x}_{0}} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}{|}_{{z}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}28 & 44 \\ 18 & 24\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
